label: Australian Milking Zebu

about.text: A composite dairy breed developed by CSIRO in Australia in the mid-1950s for hot climates. It was built from Sahiwal and Red Sindhi cattle crossed with Jersey and other European breeds, and selected for heat tolerance, tick resistance and milk. Cows are reported to give about 2,700 kg of milk per lactation.

sources.text: Origin, parent breeds, selection goals and the 2,700 kg per lactation figure taken from the Wikipedia article (fetched). The article gives no population or status.

facts.v: Built from Sahiwal and Red Sindhi cattle from Pakistan, crossed with Jersey, with some Illawarra, Guernsey and Friesian blood.

sources.text: From the Wikipedia article's account of the breed's parent stocks (fetched).

That page returned HTTP 403, so the conflict is recorded but not resolved. No population, DAD-IS risk status, composition, or year for the yield was found.
